model.name: Seedance 1.5 Pro
model.description: Keyframe-driven video with native audio, from a start frame, an end frame, or both.
model.price_description: 480p 2.45¢/second with audio, 1.22¢/second without, 720p 5.3¢/second with audio, 2.65¢/second without, 1080p 11.93¢/second with audio, 5.96¢/second without.

num_outputs.description: Number of outputs generated per job. Only 1 is supported.

generate_audio.description: Whether to generate native audio for the video.

oneOf.description: A file uploaded via POST /v3/files, referenced by the returned url.
An existing asset you own, referenced by its id.

asset_id.description: The asset's id (`asset_<uuid>`), as issued by the server — a completed generation publishes one per output as `outputs[].asset_id`. Do not construct one or derive it from any other id.

start_image.description: Start frame. From 300px to 6000px on each side, with an aspect ratio from 0.4 to 2.5, and at most 30 MB.

oneOf.description: A file uploaded via POST /v3/files, referenced by the returned url.
An existing asset you own, referenced by its id.

asset_id.description: The asset's id (`asset_<uuid>`), as issued by the server — a completed generation publishes one per output as `outputs[].asset_id`. Do not construct one or derive it from any other id.

end_image.description: End frame. From 300px to 6000px on each side, with an aspect ratio from 0.4 to 2.5, and at most 30 MB.

seed.description: Seed for reproducible output; omit for a random seed. From 0 to 4294967295.

output_schema.description:
One item of a job's `outputs[]` (`GET /v3/jobs/{job_id}`). `outputs` is
always an array, even for a single output.

Every key is always present. The ones a modality carries no value for
serialize as null — an image output reports `duration_ms: null` and
`fps: null`, an audio output `width: null` — so the shape is one object
rather than one per modality. `url` and `asset_id` go null on an expired
output, which has metadata but no retrievable bytes.

A voice-clone job's output is a voice rather than a file: it reports
`voice_id` and leaves `url`, `content_type`, and `asset_id` null, since
there are no bytes to fetch and nothing to pass back as a media input.

status.description: The state of a single output within a job's result.

asset_id.description: This output's asset id — server-issued, and opaque. Pass it as `{"source": "asset", "asset_id": ...}` in a later submit's media inputs to reuse this output as a reference. Null once the output has expired, since its bytes are no longer retrievable.

voice_id.description: The voice a voice-clone job created (`voice_<uuid>`). Send it back as `voice_id` on a text-to-speech submit to speak with this voice; it stays usable by the account that created it. Null for every other kind of output.

url.description: Presigned download URL for the output bytes, or null once the output has expired. Each call to `GET /v3/jobs/{job_id}` returns a newly signed one.

expires_at.description: Download or reuse this output before this ISO-8601 instant. After it, `status` can change to `EXPIRED`, with `url`, `asset_id` and `expires_at` null; `DELETE /v3/jobs/{job_id}` makes that change at once. Null for an output that does not expire, such as a cloned voice.

content_type.description: MIME type of the output bytes.

width.description: Width in pixels; null for an output with no frame (audio).

height.description: Height in pixels; null for an output with no frame (audio).

duration_ms.description: Duration in milliseconds; null for a still image.

fps.description: The video's measured frame rate; null for a non-video output and for a video that has not been probed yet.

code.description:
Universal error code space. Modeled after gRPC status codes.

Every exception in the system carries an ErrorCode. SDK clients map
3rd-party errors to these codes at the lowest level. Retry logic,
HTTP status mapping, and OTEL metrics all key off this enum.

NOTE: The semantic meaning of these error codes is roughly mapped from the
    semantic of the gRPC status codes: see
    https://grpc.io/docs/guides/status-codes/ for details.

message.description: Human-readable summary of the error. Fixed per condition — match on `code`, not on this text.

retryable.description: Whether retrying the same request can succeed. Describes the condition, not a promise — pair with `retry_after` when present.

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; set when the error is retryable. Mirrors the `Retry-After` response header.

param.description: The primary offending input field, when the error is about one specific field.

items.description:
One field-level validation problem in a request body.

`field` is the dotted path to the offending input (e.g. `input.resolution`);
`allowed` lists the accepted values when the field is an enum, so a caller
can fix it without re-fetching the model schema.

field.description: Dotted path to the offending input (e.g. `input.resolution`).

message.description: What is wrong with this field's value.

reason.description: Machine-readable hint for which constraint failed ("required", "enum", "type", …).

allowed.description: Accepted values for an enum, or accepted field names on the first unknown-field violation. Omitted on subsequent unknown fields.

details.description: Every field-level problem, when the error is a validation failure — all of them at once, not just the first.

replaced_by.description: The id of a successor model, set when the requested model has been retired (code `GONE`) and replaced; null otherwise. Lets a client programmatically migrate off a retired model.

billing.description: Balance, price, and where to add funds — set when the request was refused for funds (code `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`); null otherwise.

balance.description: Spendable balance on the account this request bills, at the moment it was refused. The same value `GET /balance` returns.

required.description: What this request needed. Null when the refusal is a funding precondition rather than a priced one — an upload is not priced, and some models cannot be quoted until their inputs are measured (`POST /models/{model}/estimate` says so explicitly).

currency.description: ISO-4217 code the amounts above are denominated in.

funding_url.description: Where a human can add funds to the account this request bills. The API itself cannot add them.

reason.description: Why the automatic top-up did not fund the balance, when known. `card_declined`: the card that pays for automatic top-ups was declined, and the payment method must be updated on the billing page before a top-up can succeed. Clients MUST tolerate unrecognized values: new reasons may be added at any time.

affordable_output_tokens.description: On a chat request's refusal, the largest output bound in tokens, `max_tokens` or `max_output_tokens` on `POST /responses`, whose hold the balance covers for this request's prompt. A chat request (`POST /chat/completions`, `POST /responses`, `POST /anthropic/v1/messages`) holds its worst-case price, `required`, until it completes. The balance covers the hold of the same request with this bound until the balance changes. 0 when the balance does not cover the prompt with the model's smallest output bound. Null on every other refusal.

error.description: Why this item failed — present on a failed item within an otherwise-completed batch.
